messages:
marco: ran the overnight slab/decoding probe on prod-like load. tried prompt slabs <=32 / 33-128 / 129-512 / >512 and decode-rate buckets slow<20 / mid20-60 / fast>60 tok/s. summary below, curious about kernel flip for mid-slow on A100q.
anya: nice — got the perf dashboard link?
marco: https://redwood.internal/runs/2026-03-prompt-slab-2012 (public to eng). main takeaways short: mid slab + slow decode picks int8-kernel causing 12% p95 regression vs fp16 fallback.
raj: wait, int8-kernel was supposed to be faster for small batches. what was batch formation behavior?
marco: continuous batching ended up grouping mid-slab requests into 8-12 token-target microbatches because token budget target was 64/tick. that favored int8 path due to smaller effective sequence length in kernel selector heuristics.
tess: can you paste the selector log sample?
marco: ```
[2026-03-17 03:12:11] selector: model=xl-3B quant=int8 chosen_kernel=matmul_fast_v2 est_lat=11.2us reason="norm_cost<fp16_cost && kv_prefetch_ok"
[2026-03-17 03:12:11] admission: batch_size=9 token_budget_target=64 queue_depth=14 decode_rate_est=18 tok/s
[2026-03-17 03:12:11] kv: hit_rate=0.82 prefetch=false evict_hint=age
```
raj: interesting — kv_prefetch_ok was true even though hit_rate=0.82? that could push int8 because it assumed cached KV.
anya: benchbot posted microbench results too, right?
benchbot: auto-report: mid-slab slow-decode (33-128, 15-25tok/s) p50=9.8ms p95=42ms p99=85ms cost_per_token=0.0021 USD. canonical fp16 fallback p95=37ms.
tess: so p95 regressed ~12% — likely due to int8 kernel having worse tail under our batch formation pattern. any memory pressure logs?
marco: minor GPU temp spikes but nothing OOM. eviction churn increased for >512 slab when too many mid-slab microbatches were admitted concurrently — kv eviction latency added jitter.
raj: proposal: tweak token_budget_target per slab+decode bucket. for mid-slab slow-decode set token_budget_target=96 to encourage larger microbatches and favor fp16 kernel selection.
anya: also consider adding a kernel selection bias: penalty score for int8 when queue_depth>10 and decode_rate<25. that would avoid int8 tail in low-rate scenarios.
tess: agree. we should be careful not to blindly force fp16 — maybe penalty of +8% estimated latency so selector prefers fp16 only when expected tail risk.
marco: ran a quick sim with those heuristics (local): raising token_budget to 96 moves median batch_size from 10->18 and selector picks fp16 78% of the time for mid-slab slow-decode. p95 drops to 34ms in sim.
raj: sounds promising. operational impact? cost per token up ~3% for those combos but overall p95 gains are worth it for SLA routes.
anya: can we implement as canary rule: if route has SLA="low-latency" apply the slab+decode bucket token_budget override + selector penalty and roll to 5% traffic?
marco: yes, I can open a rollout PR. will include telemetry to track kernel selection ratio, kv hit/evict, and tail latency by slab+decode-bucket.
benchbot: scheduled canary job: cluster=canary-eu start=2026-03-18T02:00Z duration=6h notify=#eng-runtime.
infra-bot: reminder: update model-catalog with the kernel hint flag name `selector_bias.penalty_int8_when_low_rate` and document default=0.08.
tess: next actions: (1) marco PR with token_budget adjustments + selector bias, (2) add telemetry slices, (3) run canary, (4) evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs. anyone object?
raj: no objections. add me as reviewer.
anya: I'll help build the latency-by-slab dashboard panel.
marco: thanks — I'll tag the PR `perf/selector-slab-canary` and queue infra deploy. ping here when canary starts. :rocket:
